rationale: The pain is real and buyers (technical founders, dev teams at SPA-based directories and marketplaces) demonstrably pay — Prerender.io at $100–500/month is the proof of willingness to pay. However, building a competitive dynamic rendering / SSR proxy service requires server infrastructure, headless browser management (Puppeteer/Playwright clusters), caching layers, and scaling logic that is far beyond Claude prompts and a Stripe link; buildability scores 3 and operational autonomy scores 3 because every new customer needs their domain configured, proxy routing set up, and ongoing infrastructure managed. These two critical build gates are well below their floors, and the total at 5.4 sits below the validate threshold anyway.
solution_plan: This is not viable for a solo non-technical operator. The product is essentially a managed rendering proxy — spinning up headless Chromium instances to pre-render SPA pages for Googlebot. This requires DevOps expertise, server infrastructure management, and per-customer configuration work. Prerender.io and Rendertron exist precisely because this is an infrastructure problem, not a prompt-engineering problem. A Claude factory cannot substitute for that infrastructure. Do not pursue.
notes: Fails buildability_with_ai floor (3 < 6) and operational_autonomy floor (3 < 7). Total also below min_total_to_validate. Drop.
